reasoning: R4 proved the legacy object is a valid LZ4 frame and produced readable decompressed bytes, so R5 does not treat compression as the unresolved layer.
R4's legacy parser required each NDJSON record to be a top-level object and returned zero records, so a different JSON root/container shape is a narrower hypothesis than corruption.
R4 proved modern /events/* values are arrays whose members include both object and string types.
Official Hyperliquid documentation states node_fills matches API fill format and node_fills_by_block is produced with --write-fills --batch-by-block, while --batch-by-block wraps events per block.
Therefore a line-delimited event array containing one string and one fill-like object is the primary R5 hypothesis, but this remains an inference until R5 evidence exists.
